_note: Nationwide scenic train views, the catalogue behind the homepage view picker. Only status 'live' is shown to readers. Everything else is a candidate: which side, which section and which season are left null until verified (viewshed from OpenStreetMap track geometry + GSI elevation, then checked against real footage). Never publish a side that has not been verified — one wrong 'sit on the right' costs the whole site's credibility. Images are generated (illustrative) and labelled as such wherever shown.

notes: The train reverses at Deyama signal station, Ohiradai Station and Kami-Ohiradai signal station. Your physical window stays beside you while its left/right label changes with the train’s direction. For the two highlighted valley sections, the terrain model points to the left as you board at Hakone-Yumoto or Gora. The window with the view can vary elsewhere along the line.
Between Tonosawa and Deyama the line crosses the Hayakawa on the Deyama bridge, high above the river: a view from both sides, gone in seconds.

Woods line much of the track. The model finds where the ground falls away on one side, not where the trees open; the view comes and goes through the leaves. Hydrangeas grow on both sides in June and July.

views.name: The Hozu gorge, Hozukyo to Kameoka
views.season: Autumn leaves mid-November to early December; cherry blossom early April
views.basis: terrain model, matching a published description (All About): the river 10–30 m below on that side

notes: The line crosses the river near Torokko Hozukyo, so the gorge switches sides: on the left from Arashiyama to Hozukyo, then on the right to Kameoka, going from Saga — the longer stretch. Coming back from Kameoka it is the other way round: on the left most of the way, then on the right after Hozukyo.

Seats are four-person boxes, A to D; the window seats are A and D. Going to Kameoka, C and D face forward; going to Saga, A and B do. Online you can choose the car and the seat: take an even-numbered box for the long stretch of gorge in either direction — D going to Kameoka, A going to Saga, for the window facing forward.
The current trains run until 29 December 2026. New cars start on 1 March 2027, when times and fares may change — we will update this page then.
routes.verification: Side and sections from a terrain model (GSI 10 m elevation, OSM track followed rail by rail): the gorge counts as in view where the ground falls 10 m or more to the river within 200 m on one side and no nearer bank hides it. The order — left first, then right after the crossing near Hozukyo — matches All About’s published account; one other guide gives the halves the other way round. Seats from Sagano Scenic Railway's own seat guide and FAQ: A and D are the window seats, C and D face forward going to Kameoka, A and B going to Saga. The even-numbered boxes are on the side of the line that has the gorge for the long stretch, reading the official seat chart against the direction of travel.

page.title: Sagano Romantic Train: Which Side for the Hozu Gorge?
page.description: Torokko Saga to Kameoka: the Hozu river is on the left as far as Hozukyo, then on the right — the longer stretch — all the way to Kameoka. A terrain model, a map and the minutes from the 2026 timetable.
page.h1: Sagano Romantic Train: which side for the gorge?

ticketGuide.verdict: Book ahead, especially in autumn. For the gorge on the long stretch, sit in an even-numbered box.

options.buy: Station windows sell that day's seats, first come, first served

faq.q: Which seat should I book on the Sagano Romantic Train?
faq.a: On the 2026 fleet, which retires on December 29, choose a window in an even-numbered box for the longer stretch of gorge. Take D going to Kameoka or A going to Saga to face forward. Odd-numbered boxes have the river between Arashiyama and Hozukyo. Check the operator's seat map for the new trains from March 1, 2027.

faq.q: Can I choose my seat?
faq.a: Yes, online: Sagano Scenic Railway's booking site shows a seat map for the train you pick. Seats can be changed up to three times, on the same train, until 23:59 the day before.

notes: After Shibaura-futo the line climbs a full circle onto the Rainbow Bridge, then crosses it on the lower deck: water on both sides, the city behind you going to Odaiba. On the loop the view swings round, so it is not given a side.
The line has no driver. The seats at the very front (and back) of the train look straight down the track — the best view of the loop and the bridge, if you can get them.

Buildings are not in the model, and in Tokyo they hide much of the water. We only count open water at least 400 m across that comes within 300 m of the line, so canals do not count — but a warehouse or a hotel can still stand in the way.
Cars mostly have long bench seats along the sides.

ticketGuide.verdict: Book the trolley on the Kurobe Gorge Railway website, or buy a same-day ticket at Unazuki. From Tokyo, ride the Hokuriku Shinkansen to Kurobe-Unazukionsen, then the Toyama Chiho Railway to Unazuki-Onsen.

options.buy: Kurobe Gorge Railway ticket (official website, or same day at Unazuki)

faq.q: Is the Kurobe Gorge Railway open all the way to Keyakidaira?
faq.a: Yes, since October 1, 2026, after repairs from the 2024 Noto earthquake. At Keyakidaira only the station area and the visitor centre are open while repairs continue. Trains to Keyakidaira run until November 30; from December 1 to 6 they turn back at Sasadaira.

faq.q: Open car or windowed car?
faq.a: The open cars have no windows: the best for photos, but cold and wet in bad weather. The Relax cars have windows you can open and seats that turn to face forward. Either way, sit on the right going up as far as Kanetsuri.

faq.q: Does the JR Pass cover the Kurobe Gorge Railway?
faq.a: No. It is a private railway, so you need its own ticket. The JR Pass does cover the Hokuriku Shinkansen to Kurobe-Unazukionsen.

faq.q: Which side is the sea on?
faq.a: For the coast between Akita-Shirakami and Ajigasawa, choose the right-hand window facing forward when the train first leaves Akita. After the reversal at Higashi-Noshiro, the same window is on the left in the direction of travel. From Aomori, choose the left-hand window at departure. After the reversal at Hirosaki, that window is on the right in the direction of travel.

faq.q: Does the JR Pass cover the Resort Shirakami?
faq.a: Yes. It is a JR East rapid train. All ordinary seats are reserved, so reserve one before you board; with the pass the reservation is included.

faq.q: Does it run every day?
faq.a: In November 2026 the trains used here run daily. From December to February they run only on set dates, so check JR East for your day.

faq.q: Which side should I sit on from Biei to Furano?
faq.a: Choose the left for the Tokachi mountain range on a clear day. Coming back towards Biei, it is on the right. Flower fields and crops vary by place and season, so there is no verified single best side for lavender.

faq.q: Does the Furano-Biei Norokko still run?
faq.a: No. JR Hokkaido states that its final run was September 23, 2026. Do not plan a 2027 trip around the Norokko timetable.

faq.q: What replaces the Norokko in 2027?
faq.a: JR Hokkaido plans the Blue Star 'Hill Colors' train between Asahikawa and Furano from July 1, 2027, on selected dates through September. Its October 2026 announcement lists the dates and planned stops and times. It also lists a separate limited express on selected June dates.

faq.q: Does the JR Pass cover the Furano Line?

faq.q: Which side is the Sea of Okhotsk on?

faq.q: When does Ryuhyo Monogatari run in 2027?
faq.a: JR Hokkaido has confirmed January 30–31 and February 1–28, 2027. March service is planned, but its exact dates were still unpublished on November 18, 2026. It is seasonal and all seats are reserved.

faq.q: Are the times on this page for Ryuhyo Monogatari?

faq.q: Will I definitely see drift ice?

faq.q: Does the JR Pass cover the Senmo Line?

faq.q: Which side is best on the Tadami Line?
faq.a: There is no single best side for the whole trip. Towards Koide, the First Tadami River Bridge is on the left, the valley after Aizu-Miyashita is on the right, it returns to the left around Hayato, then appears on the right after Aizu-Mizunuma. The sides reverse towards Aizu-Wakamatsu.

faq.q: Can I ride straight from Aizu-Wakamatsu to Koide?
faq.a: Yes, but only a few through trains run each day and some have long station waits. This page uses local 427D towards Koide and local 426D towards Aizu-Wakamatsu from JR East's November 2026 timetable. Check the official timetable for your date.

faq.q: When are the autumn leaves on the Tadami Line?
faq.a: JR East gives late October to mid-November as the usual period. It varies by year, and weather can hide the view, so treat this as a guide rather than a guarantee.

faq.q: Is there a recommended seat letter?
faq.a: No verified seat letter is given here. The river changes sides, and JR East's scenic information does not assign a seat letter. Use the section-by-section left/right timeline instead.

faq.q: Does the JR Pass cover the Tadami Line?
faq.a: Yes. The Tadami Line is operated by JR East and is within the JR network covered by the nationwide Japan Rail Pass, subject to the pass's normal validity conditions.
